ai.description: *Raorchestes kadalarensis* is a small shrub frog (SVL 20–24 mm). It features a yellowish-brown dorsum with dark brown blotches and distinct, bright yellow webbing between the fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes kadalarensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or cream-colored patch on its groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes kadalarensis* is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests and adjacent grasslands of the Munnar landscape in the Western Ghats, typically above 1,600 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes kadalarensis* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the night to forage for small insects among the vegetation of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes kadalarensis* exhibits direct development with terrestrial egg-laying. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with clutches typically containing 10–15 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes kadalarensis* is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests of the Munnar region in Kerala, located within the Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes kadalarensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched "tink" notes emitted from vegetation in high-altitude shola forest habitats.
